root_cause: get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation resolve string (forward-ref) annotations against getattr(call, '__globals__'). For a functools.wraps wrapper defined in another module, __annotations__ is copied verbatim from the original function, but __globals__ belongs to the wrapper's module. So 'ForwardRefModel' is looked up in the wrong namespace: a NameError for params, and an unresolved ForwardRef response_model for the return annotation.
best_solution: Do what typing.get_type_hints does: follow __wrapped__ to the original function before reading __globals__. In both get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation, set unwrapped = inspect.unwrap(call) and use globalns = getattr(unwrapped, '__globals__', {}). Keep inspect.signature(call) as is, since signature already follows __wrapped__. inspect.unwrap handles chains of wrappers (the test double-wraps). The return-annotation function uses the same getattr(call, '__globals__') pattern and has to be fixed too, because FastAPI builds response_model from the return annotation.
acceptable_alternatives: A manual `while hasattr(f, '__wrapped__'): f = f.__wrapped__` loop is equivalent to inspect.unwrap, as long as it is applied in BOTH get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation (or in one shared helper that both call).
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_wrapped_method_forward_reference.py::test_wrapped_method_type_inference plus the helper module tests/forward_reference_type.py, which defines forwardref_method(input: 'ForwardRefModel') -> 'ForwardRefModel' BEFORE class ForwardRefModel. The test registers passthrough(f) and passthrough(passthrough(f)) with app.post, then POSTs {'input': {'x': 0}} to both. Both responses must be {'x': 1}. The string return annotation must therefore resolve too, otherwise serialize_response raises PydanticUserError: TypeAdapter[Annotated[ForwardRef('ForwardRefModel'), ...]] is not fully defined.
locating_signals: The statement names get_typed_signature and globalns explicitly and points to typing.get_type_hints' __wrapped__ dereference. Its traceback leads to fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. The sibling get_typed_return_annotation is NOT named, but it sits a few lines below and uses the identical getattr(call, "__globals__", {}) line, so grepping __globals__ finds it. Linked issue #5065's repro has `-> "MyModel"`, which exercises the return path.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 all false). v4 (73 calls, 128s) and v8 (58 calls, 166s) submitted empty patches. v6 (15 calls) and v7 (29 calls) each patched only get_typed_signature, using a correct while-__wrapped__ loop, and left get_typed_return_annotation on getattr(call, '__globals__'). In the hidden test the request body parsed and the endpoint ran, returning ForwardRefModel(x=1). The response then failed in serialize_response with PydanticUserError, because response_model was still the unresolved ForwardRef('ForwardRefModel'). Both agents' own tests called get_typed_signature directly (v7's test could not fail at all, since it used same-module globals), so neither run tested the return-annotation or end-to-end HTTP path. v6 also wrote its test to the same path as the hidden test file.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement blames one expression in one function (here getattr(call, '__globals__')), grep the package for that exact expression and fix every sibling occurrence. Parallel code paths such as parameter vs return annotation, or request vs response, usually share the bug and the hidden test hits all of them. Write the repro end to end, exactly as the statement or linked issue shapes it: here, a string annotation on both the param and the return, a function in a separate module, and a real request through the public API. Unit-testing only the named helper passed here while the real failure was still there. Prefer the stdlib primitive the statement cites (inspect.unwrap, mirroring typing.get_type_hints) over hand-rolled loops. Never submit an empty patch after a long exploration: a partial fix scores the same as nothing, but it may pass.
